invariants: Seven actual shared-physical-workspace Source/native/extracted observations retain complete stat/lstat/type/size/version and raw device/inode/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs fields.
Windows versions use native ChangeTime rather than Python3.8 creation time, and preserve 100-nanosecond file timestamps without a float round trip.
Public stat/lstat includes the actual directory size. listDir directory size remains absent as in Source.
Win32 metadata queries retain volume serial, file index and file size, request read attributes and share read/write/delete, and always close their owned handle.
256 actual successful probes and two controlled native-query failure boundaries retain identical before/after handle counts and exactly one CloseHandle on each failure.
Full public/raw values, actual imported bytes, selected runtime, physical workspace, Source identity, extracted receipt and mandatory-lane refusal controls remain strict.
identity: The complete ordered JSON rows compare literally on the same physical paths. No timestamp, inode, directory-size or diagnostic field is normalized away.
ownership: Each successful CreateFileW handle is closed in finally, including GetFileInformationByHandle and GetFileInformationByHandleEx failures.
ordering: Existing path/type classification is followed by native metadata capture. Metadata-only changes remain visible to version guards; the selected observers do not infer arbitrary concurrent path replacement atomicity.
errors: Missing paths retain the existing FsLocal contract. Actual metadata-query failures propagate; no retry, fallback to stale creation time or new Source defect predicate is added.
cancellation: Existing filesystem cancellation checks remain in place; the synchronous scoped metadata handle is released before return or error.
adaptation: Python3.8 ctypes supplies Win32 file metadata unavailable through os.stat. Only longstanding Windows APIs are used; actual Windows7 runtime certification is user-deferred.
open_questions: Arbitrary concurrent rename/reparse/permissions and non-observed filesystem/error schedules remain in the broader tool/profile contracts.
The original WinError1175 holder/cause is not identified by these successful metadata observations; no causality or Win7 certificate is inferred.
